title: Julia Set
comment: Julia Set — Classic reference: Gaston Julia, Memoire sur l'iteration des fonctions rationnelles, 1918. Julia sets are attraction basins of iterated complex maps. The best-known example is quadratic polynomials. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_set

title: Zonohedra
comment: Zonohedra — Zonohedra are images of the l^inf ball by linear map while symmetric polyhedra are images of the l1 ball. Zonoids are the limits of zonohedra. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zonohedron
alt_text: Zonohedra. Zonohedra are images of the l^inf ball by linear map while symmetric polyhedra are images of the l1 ball. Zonoids are the limits of zonohedra.

title: Lloyd
comment: Lloyd — Classic reference: Stuart Lloyd, Least squares quantization in PCM, 1982. Continuous counterpart of k-means. Optimizes the optimal quantization energy, which is an optimal transport distance to free Dirac masses. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd%27s_algorithm
alt_text: Lloyd. Classic reference: Stuart Lloyd, Least squares quantization in PCM, 1982. Continuous counterpart of k-means. Optimizes the optimal quantization energy, which is an optimal transport distance to free Dirac masses.

title: Multipole
comment: Multipole — Large-scale N-body simulations require the evaluation of sums involving long-range interaction kernels. Fast multipoles and Barnes-Hut methods approximate these sums in n log(n) operations instead of n^2. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N-body_simulation

title: Hypotrochoids
